Explore Forecasting Solutions ↗ Talk to Our Experts ↗ PREDICTIVE BUSINESS INTELLIGENCE From Data to Decisions ↗ BUSINESS INTELLIGENCE 01 Using Historical Data to Estimate Future Business Demand Demand and sales forecasting is the process of estimating future product or service requirements and predicting sales volumes over a defined period. It involves analyzing historical sales records, customer purchasing behaviour, seasonal variations and market conditions to identify patterns that influence future demand. Businesses use these forecasts to determine how much inventory to maintain, how to schedule production, when to allocate resources and how to prepare for changes in customer requirements. At SRG Tech, we develop data-driven forecasting models that help organizations convert historical information into actionable business insights. OPERATIONAL PLANNING & OPTIMIZATION How Demand Forecasting Supports Business Operations Accurate demand forecasting provides organizations with better visibility into future requirements. It supports planning across inventory, production, resource allocation and customer management. 01 / 05 Inventory Optimization Estimate future product requirements to maintain appropriate stock levels, minimize excess inventory and reduce the risk of stock shortages. ↗ 02 / 05 Resource Allocation Use anticipated demand to plan workforce requirements, production capacity, marketing activities and distribution resources. ↗ 03 / 05 Cost Management Identify potential overstocking and understocking situations to support better purchasing decisions and reduce avoidable operational expenses. ↗ 04 / 05 Customer Demand Planning Understand expected purchasing patterns and improve product availability to meet customer requirements. ↗ 05 / 05 Market Trend Analysis Identify historical patterns, seasonal variations and changing demand trends to support informed business planning. ↗ FORECAST MODEL DEVELOPMENT A Structured Process for Generating Reliable Forecasts Developing an effective forecasting solution requires more than applying a prediction algorithm. It involves understanding the data, selecting suitable analytical methods, evaluating model performance and continuously monitoring results. STEP 01 Data Collection Collect historical sales records, transaction information, customer behaviour, market trends and other relevant business data. STEP 02 Data Preprocessing Clean and organize datasets by addressing missing values, inconsistent records and outliers to prepare reliable input data. STEP 03 Exploratory Data Analysis Examine historical data to identify trends, seasonal patterns, demand fluctuations and relationships between relevant variables. STEP 04 Forecasting Method Selection Select appropriate statistical and machine learning techniques based on the data characteristics and forecasting requirements. STEP 05 Model Development Develop and train forecasting models using historical datasets to estimate future demand and sales volumes. STEP 06 Model Evaluation Measure forecasting performance by comparing predicted values with actual results using appropriate evaluation metrics. STEP 07 Forecast Generation Generate future sales and demand estimates across selected products, categories, locations or business periods. STEP 08 Monitoring & Feedback Monitor forecast performance and update models as new data becomes available and market conditions change. STEP 09 Business Integration Integrate forecasting outputs into inventory management, supply chain planning, production scheduling and business intelligence systems. MEASURING PREDICTIVE PERFORMANCE Evaluating the Accuracy of Forecasting Models Forecasting accuracy is an important factor in determining how useful a predictive model is for business planning. Model evaluation involves comparing forecasted values against actual observations to measure prediction errors and identify opportunities for improvement. At SRG Tech, we consider appropriate statistical evaluation metrics to assess model performance and support the selection of suitable forecasting approaches. Why these metrics matter: Compare forecasting model performance. Identify prediction errors. Evaluate alternative forecasting methods. Support model improvement and selection. Key Forecast Evaluation Metrics MAE Mean Absolute Error Measures the average absolute difference between predicted values and actual observations.
